mergers_acquisitions.counterparty: Fidelity BancShares (N.C.), Inc. / The Fidelity Bank
mergers_acquisitions.terms: All-cash deal, ~$142.8 million aggregate value; $23.00 per share in cash (subject to adjustment based on adjusted stockholders' equity)
mergers_acquisitions.note: Definitive merger agreement executed March 30, 2026; Affinity shareholders approved the deal at a special meeting July 7, 2026; expected to close Q3 2026. Multi-step merger structure with Affinity Bank ultimately merging into Fidelity Bank.

mergers_acquisitions.terms: All-cash transaction, ~$89.8 million total consideration; $26.40 per share in cash
mergers_acquisitions.note: Merger agreement signed Oct 29, 2025; deal closed and became effective March 12, 2026. IF Bancorp merged into ServBanc, with ServBanc as the surviving entity. Deal is already completed as of screening date.

mergers_acquisitions.counterparty: FONAR LLC / FONAR Acquisition Sub, Inc. (acquisition group led by CEO Timothy Damadian, 57 members)
mergers_acquisitions.terms: Going-private cash-out merger: $19.00/share for common stock, $6.34/share for Class C shares, $10.50/share for Class A preferred; ~31.5% premium to pre-announcement closing price
mergers_acquisitions.note: Agreement signed Dec 23, 2025; shareholders approved at special meeting May 28, 2026; deal expected to close June 3, 2026 (i.e., already completed by screening date). Company expected to delist from Nasdaq as a CEO-led take-private transaction.

mergers_acquisitions.terms: $25.00 per share in cash, ~$1.272 billion transaction value
mergers_acquisitions.note: Merger agreement signed April 13-14, 2026; deal closed and completed July 27, 2026. Avanos is now a private company and its stock has ceased trading on the NYSE.

mergers_acquisitions.terms: $33.50 per share in cash (raised from an initial proposal of $25.75/share on Feb 5, 2026), all-cash deal valued at approximately $2.2 billion
mergers_acquisitions.note: Dream Finders made an unsolicited proposal in February 2026; a definitive merger agreement was subsequently reached. Deal pending stockholder and regulatory approval; PREM14A/DEFM14A filings indicate the deal is proceeding toward a shareholder vote as of Sept 2026.

mergers_acquisitions.counterparty: Smith Ventures (fintech assets) and CommerceOne Financial Corporation (bank)
mergers_acquisitions.terms: Two-part breakup: Smith Ventures acquires/privatizes the non-bank fintech business; CommerceOne acquires Green Dot Bank, becoming a new public bank holding company. Total implied value to shareholders ~$14.23-$19.18/share; aggregate deal value $825M-$1.1B, including $470M cash distribution to shareholders.
mergers_acquisitions.note: Announced Nov 24, 2025. Shareholders of both Green Dot and CommerceOne approved the transaction at special meetings on June 23, 2026; deal was expected to close around Q2 2026. Effectively splits and privatizes/restructures the company - current market cap is not a clean 'value' signal.

mergers_acquisitions.terms: All-stock deal valued at approximately $448.1 million; Blue Ridge shareholders receive 0.086 HomeTrust shares per Blue Ridge share
mergers_acquisitions.note: Merger agreement signed Aug 16, 2026; expands HomeTrust into Virginia markets, creating a combined bank with over $7 billion in assets. Deal not yet complete as of screening date. HomeTrust is the acquirer, so this dilutes/changes its share count and balance sheet meaningfully.

mergers_acquisitions.counterparty: Safe Harbor Marinas (Blackstone Infrastructure portfolio company)
mergers_acquisitions.terms: $53.00 per share in cash, all-cash deal valued at approximately $1.5 billion (96% premium to Jan 30, 2026 closing price of $27.03)
mergers_acquisitions.note: Definitive merger agreement announced Aug 10, 2026; deal unanimously approved by MarineMax board, not contingent on financing, expected to close by end of 2026 pending shareholder/regulatory approval. Stock trading near deal price makes current valuation essentially merger arb, not a value signal.

mergers_acquisitions.terms: NAV-for-NAV merger, ~$220M total; each SWKH share converted into 1.7264 RWAY shares or $20.59 cash (holder election), plus $0.74 cash pro rata guaranteed payment.
mergers_acquisitions.note: Definitive merger agreement announced October 14, 2025; approved by SWK shareholders March 31, 2026; deal closed April 6, 2026 and SWKH was delisted from Nasdaq.

mergers_acquisitions.terms: All-stock merger valued at $3.6B; American Woodmark shareholders received 5.150 shares of MasterBrand common stock for each AMWD share.
mergers_acquisitions.note: Agreement signed August 5, 2025; FTC closed its investigation and HSR waiting period expired May 22, 2026; merger completed May 28, 2026, with American Woodmark now a wholly owned subsidiary of MasterBrand. AMWD no longer trades independently.

mergers_acquisitions.counterparty: Keller Companies, Inc. (parent of Kalwall Corporation and Structures Unlimited Inc.)
mergers_acquisitions.terms: Initial cash payment of $105 million at closing, plus potential earnout of up to $10 million tied to financial performance through fiscal 2027 Q3.
mergers_acquisitions.note: Apogee entered a merger agreement to acquire Keller Companies (parent of Kalwall) announced May 27, 2026. As acquirer, this is a sizeable capital deployment relative to Apogee's size that could distort near-term valuation metrics; not a threat to Apogee's own independence.

mergers_acquisitions.counterparty: LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton (Marc Jacobs business) / WHP Global
mergers_acquisitions.terms: G-III and WHP Global formed a joint venture (with a reported ~$500M brand investment plan) to acquire the Marc Jacobs business from LVMH; not disclosed in full.
mergers_acquisitions.note: Agreements announced May 14, 2026 for G-III/WHP Global JV to acquire Marc Jacobs from LVMH. Sizeable strategic transaction for G-III as acquirer/JV partner, not a threat to G-III's independence.

mergers_acquisitions.counterparty: HCB Financial Corp. (parent of Highpoint Community Bank)
mergers_acquisitions.terms: ~$70.2 million deal; each HCB share converted into $17.51 cash plus 1.5900 shares of Independent Bank common stock.
mergers_acquisitions.note: Definitive merger agreement signed March 18, 2026; shareholder and regulatory approvals obtained; acquisition completed July 1, 2026, with system integration targeted for November 9, 2026. IBCP is the acquirer, not target.

mergers_acquisitions.terms: Each HCB share converted into $17.51 cash + 1.5900 shares of Independent Bank Corporation common stock; aggregate merger consideration ~$74.9 million (~1.59M IBCP shares + $17.5M cash), total deal value reported around $116 million.
mergers_acquisitions.note: Definitive merger agreement announced March 18, 2026; regulatory approvals and shareholder approval obtained; transaction completed July 1, 2026. HCB is parent of Highpoint Community Bank (~$590M assets).

mergers_acquisitions.terms: Up to $53.30 per common share in cash: $46.57/share payable at closing plus $6.73/share contingent on repurchase of certain MFBP preferred stock within 12 months of closing. Aggregate transaction value expected to exceed $105 million (~$100M base).
mergers_acquisitions.note: Definitive merger agreement unanimously approved by both boards, announced July 22, 2026; expected to close Q4 2026. Combined institution (~$1.27B assets) expected to become the largest African American-owned financial institution in the US.

mergers_acquisitions.terms: All-stock deal: 0.3470 shares of Bank First (BFC) common stock per PSB Holdings share; deal valued at approximately $202.9 million, reported premium of more than 80% to PSB shareholders.
mergers_acquisitions.note: Agreement signed and announced ~May 20, 2026, unanimously approved by both boards; pending regulatory and PSB shareholder approval; closing and systems conversion expected Q4 2026. PSB Holdings is parent of Peoples State Bank (Wisconsin).

mergers_acquisitions.terms: All-stock deal valued at approximately $41 million; Victory shareholders received 0.5 shares of QNB common stock for each Victory share.
mergers_acquisitions.note: Announced September 23, 2025; shareholders of both companies approved the merger February 19, 2026; merger completed with Victory merging into QNB, creating a combined bank with ~$2.4 billion in assets. As acquirer QNB's own market value is somewhat affected by integration but this is a completed/near-complete deal, worth flagging as a recent major corporate action.

mergers_acquisitions.terms: Fairfax to acquire all outstanding Class A Non-Voting shares at $8.00/share and Class B Voting shares at $12.00/share; Class A price ~41% premium to closing price / ~42% premium to 20-day VWAP; equity value ~$397 million, enterprise value ~$579 million.
mergers_acquisitions.note: Arrangement agreement announced June 15, 2026; shareholders approved August 11, 2026; transaction completed August 14, 2026 -- Andrew Peller is now a private company owned by Fairfax. Stock is fully off-market at the deal price.

mergers_acquisitions.counterparty: Pure Casino Entertainment Limited Partnership (Indigenous Gaming Partners)
mergers_acquisitions.terms: All-cash acquisition at $13.65 per Gamehost common share, a ~16% premium to the March 27, 2026 closing price and ~17% premium to the 20-day VWAP.
mergers_acquisitions.note: Definitive arrangement agreement announced March 30, 2026; shareholders approved June 11, 2026; transaction closed June 24, 2026 and Gamehost shares were delisted from the TSX. Gamehost is now a private subsidiary (renamed 2825587 Alberta Ltd.) of Pure/Indigenous Gaming Partners.

mergers_acquisitions.terms: All-cash acquisition at $51.00 per Class A Limited Voting Share; enterprise value approximately $1.2 billion.
mergers_acquisitions.note: Followed an activist tender offer by Plantro Ltd. in April 2025 that triggered a strategic review and four competing preliminary takeover bids (IMCO, Northleaf, OMERS, QIC). Plenary Americas agreement announced May 19, 2026, unanimously board-approved and shareholder-approved; Saskatchewan government passed legislation (Bill 57) in May 2026 to preserve a 'Golden Share' keeping ISC's IP and head office in Saskatchewan post-close. Deal expected to close Q3 2026, taking ISC private.

other.terms: Original deal (Jan 6, 2025): Getty Images to pay $9.50 cash per Shutterstock share plus a merger-of-equals stock component; Shutterstock stockholders approved June 10, 2025; DOJ cleared the deal Feb 23, 2026, but the UK CMA required divestiture of Shutterstock's editorial business, which Getty declined to do.
other.note: Getty Images announced June 30, 2026 it would not sell Shutterstock's editorial business and terminated the merger agreement effective July 7, 2026. The deal is now dead; recent stock price action reflects post-termination standalone re-rating (potential unwind of merger-arb positioning) rather than a live corporate action, but this is very recent and highly relevant context for the value score.

other.terms: All-stock merger of ACRES Capital Corp (ACC, parent of external manager) into an ACR subsidiary; each ACC share converted into 2.61882 ACR shares; ~7.5 million new ACR shares issued to ACC stockholders; also completed a $200M 8.625% Senior Secured Notes private placement
other.note: Merger agreement dated April 29, 2026; shareholders approved June 22, 2026; transaction and internalization completed August 6, 2026. Not a buyout/going-private, but materially changes share count and cost structure, so current market cap/valuation metrics reflect a freshly reshaped capital structure rather than a stable baseline.

other.terms: Not disclosed / not yet a definitive agreement as of the reports found. Verbal take-private bids reportedly valued the company around US$1.35-1.4 billion; interested parties reported to include Boyu Capital, Advent International, Bosideng International, and a FountainVest Capital-Anta Sports consortium.
other.note: Controlling shareholder Bain Capital (majority owner since 2013) reported via Goldman Sachs-advised process to be weighing an exit / take-private sale as of August-September 2025. Status as of this screening (Sept 2026) is unclear -- no definitive agreement was found confirming a signed deal, so this should be treated as an ongoing/unresolved situation rather than a completed transaction; still material enough that GOOS's market pricing may reflect buyout speculation rather than pure fundamentals.

other.type: Going-private transaction / Nasdaq delisting via reverse stock split
other.terms: Reverse stock split at a ratio between 1-for-2,000 and 1-for-4,000; shareholders holding fewer shares than the split denominator are cashed out at $6.60 per share.
other.note: Board approved plan to delist from Nasdaq and terminate SEC reporting obligations, expected to save ~$2.4 million annually. Transaction completed around December 2025, and the stock (ticker now OTCPK:TTSH) trades OTC post-delisting -- current market pricing reflects this going-private cash-out price, not organic value.

other.terms: Sale of NetWolves Network Services LLC to COEO Solutions, LLC for $14,500,000 in cash, subject to customary post-closing adjustments.
other.note: Completed July 31, 2026 as part of a strategic refocus on core healthcare operations (VasoHealthcare/VasoMedical). A separate prior going-private merger attempt with Achari Ventures Holdings Corp (announced Dec 2023) was terminated in September 2024, so Vaso remains independently traded, but this recent divestiture is a material change to its business mix and cash position.
